I'll start by addressing the first part of your question. For me, I am incredibly self-aware and self-analytical. This helps tremendously with mental fortitude. I like to examine why I, and others, do everything and anything that I do. I do this constantly - challenging my own ideals and beliefs every second that I am making decisions. If somebody is doing a gesture or saying something, I want to know more than just that action - I want to know why. That motivation is way more important to me than the gesture. The gesture, despite how nice it was, could be completely meaningless if I am able to figure out that the reason that person did it was because of a selfish reason or out of personal gain. On the same coin, a terrible action can sometimes be excused if the person genuinely meant well.

Now, being very self-aware of mine and others intentions helps with two things - 1) it makes you realize that a lot of the things that piss you off or annoy you aren't worth getting rattled about, and 2) you can start to empathize with people more. Both of those things will help you if shit ever starts to hit the fan with a friend or coworker. I apply different methods to other things that we don't have control over, but to TL;DR that my method consists of 'you didn't have control over this, getting upset about this will not help you overcome it' and moving on from there. I don't want to write a book but that's a very short short gist of how I am mentally strong and block out meaningless distractions.
